title: DiffLiG: Diffusion-enhanced Liquid Graph with Attention Propagation for Grid-to-Station Precipitation Correction
provenance_note: The SHA-256 identifies the exact retained PDF inspected in this rapid source/argument check. Original supplied report bytes are retained locally. The original PDF retrieval timestamp is taken from matching retained metadata.
version: NeurIPS 2025 official proceedings PDF (retained local copy)
summary: The official implementation uses incompatible geographic coordinates, retains closed edges after softmax, has a constant consensus score, discards grid history and exceeds the reported parameter count in one submodule alone. Published forecast effects remain unmeasured.
impact_rationale: Minor: concrete release/method discrepancies, without evidence tying their effects to the paper’s central reported forecast results.
review_scope: Claim-focused reading of the original paper and relevant author-released passages; direct mathematical or static-source reasoning. No author program, earlier verifier, model or benchmark was executed during this check.
limitations: Preliminary AI assessment; independent human scientific adjudication remains pending.
Analytic witnesses and static release checks do not remeasure the published benchmark results.

problems.title: Geographic degrees and normalized coordinates are conflated
problems.source_location: Section 3.4 and Algorithm 1, PDF pp.5–6; Appendix J, PDF pp.33–34; MixData.py and Haversine layer methods
claim: The paper defines physical Haversine distances and geographic nearest neighbors; the release feeds min–max-normalized coordinates into a degree-based Haversine formula.
analysis: Points \((100^\circ,30^\circ)\) and \((100.125^\circ,30^\circ)\) are about \(12.0372\) km apart with Earth radius \(6371\) km. After longitude bounds \(70\)–\(140\) and latitude bounds \(15\)–\(55\), the same formula on normalized values gives about \(0.198558\) km, reversing the predicate at threshold \(0.5\). Coordinate-Euclidean ranking also differs: from \((100^\circ,50^\circ)\), candidates \((101.4^\circ,50^\circ)\) and \((100^\circ,51^\circ)\) have coordinate distances \(1.4,1\), but Haversine distances approximately \(100.063,111.195\) km, reversing the nearest neighbor.
result: The physical graph operations differ from the description. Coordinate normalization for learned embeddings remains legitimate; benchmark consequences are unresolved.
repair: Keep raw coordinates for physical distances and normalized coordinates for embeddings; rank the intended neighbors using the declared physical metric.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is retained where stated; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a local implementation or interpretation defect; damage to the central empirical result has not been established.

problems.title: Multiplying a logit by zero does not remove its edge
problems.source_location: Section 3.4, PDF p.5; GNN_Layer_External.message, lines 87–99; internal counterpart
claim: The paper multiplies normalized attention by gate and decay; the release applies softmax after multiplying the raw logits.
analysis: For logits \((-1,8)\), decays \((0.5,0.2)\), gates \((1,0)\), the source normalizes logits \((-0.5,0)\), yielding weights approximately \((0.377541,0.622459)\). The closed edge receives positive, larger mass, while the paper’s factorized expression has second coefficient exactly \(0\). All-closed groups become uniform. A hard threshold comparison converted to floating point also supplies no ordinary gradient to the threshold, despite its parameter declaration.
result: Closed edges survive aggregation and the hard threshold does not implement the described learned gate path.
repair: Apply the declared gate/decay after normalized attention with explicit neighborhood and empty-group conventions. A masked-softmax alternative requires its own specified normalization and gate-gradient rule.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is retained where stated; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: The consensus score is constant and aggregation crosses examples
problems.source_location: Section 3.6, PDF pp.6–7; selector.py, forward and score reductions
claim: The selector is described as attention across candidates, assigning a candidate-specific consensus score.
analysis: Its input \((N,M,d)\) is permuted to \((M,N,d)\) for default sequence-first attention, so stations are the sequence and candidates are batches. Averaging both station dimensions of a row-stochastic attention matrix gives \(M^{-2}\sum_{u,v}A_{nuv}=1/M\) for every candidate in evaluation mode. Thus candidates \((0,1,3)\) and \((4,2,1)\) both score \(1/3\). Other selector branches remain active. Their unsegmented averaging can also make one example depend on batch mates: candidate scores \((0,2)\) give softmax \((0.119203,0.880797)\), but adding another example with \((10,-10)\) makes the pooled logits \((5,-4)\), reversing the first example’s mixture.
result: The claimed consensus branch cannot distinguish candidates at evaluation, and global pooling can couple separate forecast examples.
repair: Use the intended candidate/station attention layout and a nonconstant, explicitly defined consensus reduction; segment independent example-level score aggregation.

problems.title: The grid branch discards every earlier timestep
claim: The described grid encoder attends over temporal input, while its active forward path selects only the final column.
analysis: Two grid nodes with histories \((1,2,3,4)\), \((5,6,7,8)\) and alternatives \((1001,1002,1003,4)\), \((1005,1006,1007,8)\) both map to \((4,8)\). Holding other inputs and randomness fixed, all downstream values in this branch agree; derivatives with respect to discarded times are zero. A temporal-attention module is constructed but unused in the active path. The separate station-history encoder remains active.
result: The release cannot use the claimed grid temporal history. This does not mean the entire model has no temporal information.
repair: Either implement/document the intended temporal encoder or state that only the final gridded field is used. No replacement architecture is established as restoring results.

problems.title: One configured submodule exceeds the reported full-model count
problems.source_location: Table 2, PDF p.7; DiffLiG_Launcher.py, line 31; SimpleGraphDiffusion constructor
claim: Table 2 reports \(49{,}361\) full-model parameters, while the launcher uses hidden width \(h=128\).
analysis: The active diffusion constructor contains three \(h\to h\) graph convolutions, two \(2h\to h\) convolutions, a \(2\to h\) position projection, an \(h\to h\) output projection and an \(h\to1\) auxiliary head. Their standard total is \(8h^2+10h+1=132{,}353\). Even the five graph-convolution matrix weights alone contain \(7h^2=114{,}688\), independent of bias or auxiliary-head conventions. Ensemble reuse does not multiply this count.
result: The released configuration cannot be the reported parameter-count configuration. The exact table-producing configuration is unknown.
repair: Identify the actual experiment configuration/checkpoint and count its instantiated parameters; no guessed replacement full-model count is supplied.
